label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_egon.mdl, models/sentry.mdl, models/floater.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, D, A, C where the asset was D, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline reads as a waist-high control console: a full-width lower box about 24 units deep, with a shorter upper block set flush to the back, as the brief's words describe. In the left and right views the upper block sits at the back of the lower one, and nothing sticks out or is missing in any of the ten views.

M2.reason: Measured size is 44 wide, 42 high and 24 deep. The brief asks for waist high at 40, so height is 5% over, inside the 15% band for a prop. No length or width was given by the brief, so the other two dimensions are not charged.

M3.reason: Every part the brief names is present: three round gold dials on the upper block's front (front view, front-left and front-right), two dark screens (front view), and a row of five switches under them (front view). The base and hazard-stripe trim are also there. The dials and switches are painted or shallowly modelled, but each reads clearly at game size.

M4.reason: The materials match the brief's palette: grey rusted steel on the upper block, blue-green-grey weathered metal on the lower body, yellow and black hazard paint along the base, and dark green-black screens. Nothing is out of the palette and no region is the wrong material.

M5.reason: Surface detail is there in its places: panel seams and vertical lines on the lower body, rust streaks and scuffs on both blocks, the hazard stripe along the base, and the screen bezels. The sharpness matches the game's own surfaces at this scale.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In the four readings of the line-up test (A to D, with the asset at D, B, B and D), the judges picked B, D, A and C, so the asset was never the one picked as not made by Valve. Three of the four readings took it for one of the game's own, which is a pass. The cap still holds at 2.

M7.reason: The front is where the brief puts it: the screens, dials and switches face the front view. The model is upright and sits flat on its base at its origin, with the hazard-stripe base on the floor.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks pass with no errors. The asset has 24 triangles, far under twice the median of 238 and under the third quartile of 291 for Half-Life's props of its kind. In all ten views the surfaces are closed, the underside is solid, and nothing floats or is inside out.
